semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: Clinical neurophysiology involves the study of nervous system function through recording bioelectrical activity, aligning it closely with electrophysiology, which studies the electrical properties of biological cells and tissues.
Clinical neurophysiology often uses neuroimaging technologies to visualize the structure and function of the nervous system.

parent_domains.justification: Neuroscience is a broad field that encompasses all study of the nervous system, which includes clinical neurophysiology as a sub-discipline.
Neurology focuses on disorders of the nervous system and is closely related to clinical neurophysiology, which measures the nervous system's function.

closest_parent_domain.justification: Clinical neurophysiology directly relates to neurology as it applies electrophysiological studies to diagnose and treat neurological disorders.

child_domains.justification: Electroencephalography (EEG) is a specific tool and technique used within clinical neurophysiology for recording electrical activity in the brain.
Neuroimaging techniques are often employed within clinical neurophysiology to investigate neural function and structure.

closest_child_domain.justification: EEG is a primary diagnostic tool used within clinical neurophysiology to measure electrical activity, directly related to clinical neurophysiological assessments.

sibling_domains.justification: Neuropsychiatry is closely related to clinical neurophysiology as it also deals with the study of disorders that have both neurological and psychological features.
Cognitive neuroscience shares an interest in how brain function impacts behavior and can overlap with clinical neurophysiology in studying brain activity.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: Cognitive neuroscience closely aligns with clinical neurophysiology in studying the neural substrates of processes underlying mental functions.

unrelated_domains.justification: Neurotopology focuses on the spatial organization of the nervous system, which is not directly related to the physiological measurements in clinical neurophysiology.
Theoretical neuroscience uses mathematics and physics to model neural systems, which is quite distinct from the clinical focus of neurophysiology.
Physiological psychology focuses on the biological basis of behavior, but it is more aligned with psychology than the clinical diagnostic focus of neurophysiology.
Visual neuroscience specializes in how neural systems process visual information, somewhat related but not central to the clinical focus.
Computational neuroscience models the brain using computational approaches and is not focused on clinical measures of neurophysiology.
